description.purpose: The TTL watchdog (R-AG-1, GH #1096). It carries no schedule of its own: ./sweep keeps one one-shot named `access-sweep` under a fixed id and re-arms it (`rearm`) for the next expires_at after every run.
description.use_when: Inside the access hive, always. It is not a poll (GH #553): a broker with no grant ahead orders nothing and stays silent.
description.not_in_scope: No cron. The expiry that matters is the comparison ./invoke makes on every call; the watchdog only has the `expired` row written at the moment the grant runs out instead of minutes later.
description.emits_meaning: A plain strike, schedule_name `access-sweep`, which is what the hive's edge recognises. A refused order leaves as `timer_op_error` and the hive's edge carries it to ./sweep.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove by schedule_id) as body.op -- in practice the one `add` with `rearm` that ./sweep sends.
examples: a grant expiring at 09:15:00.000 -> one strike at 09:15:00.001 -> ./sweep books it and arms the next
